servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q1_q: Which auctions can your marketing target?
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q1_a: All major US auto auctions, Copart, IAAI, Manheim, plus secondary platforms like ACV Auctions, Adesa, and SCA Auction. We match SEO, ad creative and landing pages to whichever auction your clients buy from most.
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q2_q: Do you actually ship cars or just market for shippers?
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q2_a: We are an AI agency, not a logistics company. We grow visibility, leads and brand for logistics companies that ship vehicles from US auctions to Georgia. Your operations team handles the actual transport.
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q3_q: How long until I see leads from your work?
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q3_a: Paid ads (Google, Meta) bring qualified leads in week 2. SEO compounds over months, first ranking improvements at week 4-6, meaningful organic traffic at month 3-4, dominant rankings by month 6.
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q4_q: Can you build the live auction feed widget for our site?
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q4_a: Yes. We integrate live Copart, IAAI and Manheim VIN feeds, visitors browse real lots on your domain, you collect leads at the highest-intent moment. Available in Acceleration and Domination tiers.
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q5_q: What does pricing actually look like?
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q5_a: Custom pricing, we quote after reviewing your current marketing, traffic, ad spend and conversion gaps. Engagements typically run 3+ months minimum because SEO and brand work compound over time.
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q6_q: Do you handle Georgian, Russian and English content?
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q6_a: All three, plus German if your client base reaches Europe. Native speakers write each version, not auto-translation. Auto-import buyers in Georgia search in all three languages depending on background.
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q7_q: What's the cost to ship a car from the US to Georgia in 2026?
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q7_a: Total landed cost typically runs 1.4, 1.7× auction price. Example: a $12,000 Copart vehicle becomes ~$17,800, $20,400 by the time it sits in Tbilisi, auction fees ($800, $1,100), US inland transport ($300, $500), sea freight Newark→Poti ($1,300, $1,600), 5% Georgia customs duty, 18% VAT and a logistics service fee. Use our calculator above for your specific number, or check official rates at https://www.rs.ge.
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q8_q: What is a salvage title and is it legal to import to Georgia?
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q8_a: A salvage title means an insurance company declared the car a total loss after damage or theft recovery. The car is fully importable and registerable in Georgia after a technical inspection, Georgian law has no salvage-specific restriction. Salvage titles are the bulk of Copart and IAAI inventory; most cars are repairable and end up on Georgian roads after rebuild. Reference: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvage_title.
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q9_q: How long does it take from auction win to delivery in Tbilisi?
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q9_a: Plan 35, 55 days end-to-end. Breakdown: 3, 7 days inland US transport from auction yard to Newark/New Jersey port, 30, 45 days sea freight to Poti, 2, 5 days customs clearance and transport to Tbilisi. Faster routes via Hamburg or Antwerp shave 5, 10 days but cost ~20% more.
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q10_q: Can I import an electric vehicle to Georgia and what are the duties?
servicesAuctionMarketing.faq_q10_a: Yes, EV imports are encouraged. Customs duty is 0% for fully electric vehicles regardless of age, versus 5% for combustion cars. VAT (18%) and excise tax still apply. Tesla, BMW i-series, Lucid and similar full-EVs from Copart and IAAI are popular Georgia imports. Hybrids (PHEV, mild-hybrid) follow the regular ICE rate.
